mission: Lock-in. Ben commits to the pursuit. The group forms because no alternative exists. The triple-layered lock-in activates: seal failing, survivors dependent, Veraine already moving.
why_now: The information is all on the table. The next move has to be chosen before the ship can lift, and Ben is the person with the keys.
conflict: Every instinct Ben has trained tells him to pick up the comm and call Luke. Every calculation he does not quite permit himself to finish tells him that the Order's response time would cost more than the survivors have. He picks the partial report and does not say the word 'help'.
turning_point: Torin asks a quiet, almost friendly question about the modern Jedi's relationship with the light/dark boundary. 'Gavran thought so too. Before.' Ben files it without processing it.
opening_hook: Ben spreads the fortress data across the command table — Corridor maps, seal readings, Veraine's file — while Sera and Torin work through the archive beside him.
closing_hook: Ben sends a partial report to Luke — enough to explain the delay, not enough to reveal the scope. The Steady Returns lifts off the plateau, pointed along the Corridor. Someone else is following them.
emotional_trajectory: Overwhelmed assessment -> grim determination -> the quiet cost of choosing to carry this alone

stakes.personal: Ben takes the weight because the choice is not really a choice to him yet — the pattern closes around him before he names it
stakes.interpersonal: The fragile group dynamic — Sera's conditional respect, Torin's warmth, Kael's distance, Desh's pragmatism
stakes.external: The clock is ticking on three fronts: seal degradation, Veraine's progress, and the Order's ignorance

setting: Fortress upper level -> departure from the uncharted world
sensory_details: The fortress shrinking below as the Steady Returns climbs off the plateau; the wrongness diffused through the wider sky now, still present but spread; five people in a ship built for two; the survivors' hands hovering above modern cockpit interfaces they do not yet recognise — Sera close but restrained, Torin observing, Kael deliberately still
canon_elements_needed: Ben Skywalker communication protocols with Luke and the Jedi Order
Jedi Order institutional hierarchy for crisis reporting
Ruusan Corridor strategic geography and anchor node network
Post-Fate of the Jedi era Jedi Order operational capacity
Force technique lineage and transmission across eras
action_beats: Ben lays out fortress data and Corridor maps across the command table
Sera and Torin organize archive materials into tactical priority order from muscle memory
Ben composes a partial report to Luke on his datapad and transmits it before he can change his mind
The Steady Returns lifts off the mountain plateau, engines straining with five passengers aboard a ship built for two
notes: R05 partial — technique lineage first surfaces. H06 planted: Torin's quiet question ('Gavran thought so too. Before.') seeds his turn fifteen chapters later — understated, easy to miss on first read, should land in Ben's memory without Ben articulating why it bothers him. Diagnostic-voice trap — Ben should not, in this scene, narrate his self-reliance as a pattern. The partial report is the behavioural evidence; his interiority should stay inside the practical math of what he can say to Luke without losing the next twenty-four hours. The phrase 'burden is mine to carry' belongs to a later chapter, earned by consequence. Relationship turns — Ben/Desh shift to co-witnesses; Sera/Torin recognise each other in the archive without language for the thousand-year ache yet; Kael stays adjacent, not yet inside.
